result.area: Failure-path behavior of /workspace/dataset/test16_executable: exit codes, byte-exact stderr tracebacks, stdout emptiness, argparse-vs-runtime error precedence

rules.rule: There are exactly three exit codes. 0 = success (including --help/-h and empty --data). 2 = any argparse error. 1 = any runtime ValueError from pyaes. No other exit code was ever observed. Exit code is the highest-priority thing to match.
rules.evidence: Exhaustive probing: success/help/empty-data -> 0; missing required, missing value, unrecognized args -> 2; Invalid key size, plaintext block must be 16 bytes -> 1.

rules.rule: On BOTH runtime failure paths stdout is byte-empty (0 bytes), verified with `od -c` on a redirected file. Nothing is ever partially printed, because `print` happens in a second loop after all encryption completes. Even with 3 blocks where blocks 1-2 encrypt fine and block 3 is short, stdout is 0 bytes.
rules.evidence: `--key aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefSHORT' >/tmp/p3.bin` -> EXIT=1, wc -c = 0, `od -c` prints only `0000000`. Same for --key short (`od -c /tmp/o1.bin` -> `0000000`, size 0).

rules.rule:
Invalid key size traceback, written to stderr verbatim (ends with a trailing newline), exit 1:
"Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test16.py", line 26, in <module>
  File "test16.py", line 11, in main
  File "pyaes/aes.py", line 304, in __init__
  File "pyaes/aes.py", line 134, in __init__
ValueError: Invalid key size
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test16' due to unhandled exception!
"
rules.evidence: Byte dump via `od -c` of stderr shows exactly this, terminating `t i o n ! \n` at offset 0000466 (310 bytes with a 3-digit pid). Frame line numbers: test16.py 26, test16.py 11, pyaes/aes.py 304, pyaes/aes.py 134.

rules.rule:
Short/long plaintext block traceback, written to stderr verbatim (trailing newline), exit 1:
"Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test16.py", line 26, in <module>
  File "test16.py", line 18, in main
  File "pyaes/aes.py", line 342, in encrypt
ValueError: plaintext block must be 16 bytes
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test16' due to unhandled exception!
"
rules.evidence: `od -c` of stderr for `--key aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data abc` ends at 0000431 with `c e p t i o n ! \n`. Frame line numbers: test16.py 26, test16.py 18, pyaes/aes.py 342 (in `encrypt`).

rules.rule: PyInstaller strips source text: every traceback frame is only the `  File "...", line N, in NAME` line with NO following source-code line. Do not emit a source line.
rules.evidence: od -c dumps show `in <module>\n  File` and `in main\n  File` adjacent with no intervening code line.

rules.rule: The `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` number is a process id and is inherently non-reproducible. It equals the pid of the forked PyInstaller child, which is the launched process pid + 1..2, and it increases monotonically across runs. Emulate with `process.pid`.
rules.evidence: Background-launched runs: launched=1492 -> PYI-1494; launched=1496 -> PYI-1497; launched=1500 -> PYI-1501; launched=1504 -> PYI-1505. Ten identical repeated runs produced PYI-1669,1673,1677,1681,1685,1689,1693,1697,1701,1705 (strictly increasing, step 4). Via `sh -c 'echo $$; exec ...'` the shell pid 1426 -> PYI-1431.

rules.rule: Key size is validated by UTF-8 BYTE length; only 16, 24, 32 bytes succeed. 0, 1, 15, 17, 23, 25, 31, 33 bytes all produce the identical `Invalid key size` traceback and exit 1 — the message never varies with how wrong the size is.
rules.evidence: Loop over key lengths 0,1,15,16,17,23,24,25,31,32,33 of 'a': exit 0 only for 16/24/32; every other length gave the byte-identical traceback (only the PYI pid differing). `--key 'éééééééé'` (8 chars / 16 bytes) -> exit 0; `--key 'éééééééééééééééé'` (16 chars / 32 bytes) -> exit 0; `--key '😀😀😀😀'` (4 chars / 16 bytes) -> exit 0.

rules.rule: Data length is validated per 16-byte slice in UTF-8 bytes. Any total byte length not a multiple of 16 fails on the final short slice with `plaintext block must be 16 bytes`, exit 1, stdout empty. Data length 0 is legal: zero iterations, zero output, exit 0.
rules.evidence: datalen 1, 15, 17, 31, 47 -> exit 1 identical traceback; datalen 0 -> exit 0 with 0 stdout bytes. `--data '0123456789abcdeé'` (16 chars, 17 UTF-8 bytes) -> exit 1; `--data 'éééééééé'` (8 chars, 16 bytes) -> exit 0 with one repr line.

rules.rule: Error precedence, strictly ordered: (1) `-h`/`--help` anywhere -> print help to stdout, exit 0, beating every other error; (2) argparse per-option error (`expected one argument`) -> exit 2; (3) argparse missing-required error -> exit 2; (4) argparse unrecognized-arguments error -> exit 2; (5) Invalid key size (source line 11) -> exit 1; (6) plaintext block must be 16 bytes (source line 18) -> exit 1.
rules.evidence: `--foo -h` -> help, exit 0. `--key -h` -> `argument --key: expected one argument`, exit 2 (help loses to the value error). `--bogus` alone -> `the following arguments are required: --key, --data` (required beats unrecognized), exit 2. `-k K --data D` -> `required: --key`, exit 2. `--key aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data abc --foo` -> `unrecognized arguments: --foo`, exit 2 (argparse beats runtime). `--key short --data abc` (both wrong) -> Invalid key size, exit 1 — key error wins regardless of flag order (`--data abc --key short` gives the same).

rules.rule: When both key and data are invalid, the key-size error always wins (it is raised on source line 11, before the encryption loop on line 18), including when data is empty. Flag order on the command line is irrelevant.
rules.evidence: `--key short --data abc` -> Invalid key size / line 11; `--data abc --key short` -> Invalid key size; `--key short --data ''` -> Invalid key size, exit 1.

rules.rule:
Every argparse error is exactly two lines on stderr, both ending in 
, stdout byte-empty: `usage: test16_executable [-h] --key KEY --data DATA
` then `test16_executable: error: <msg>
`.
rules.evidence: `od -c` of stderr for no-args ends `... - - d a t a \n` at 0000202 (130 bytes); all argparse probes showed the same two-line shape with 0-byte stdout.

rules.rule: Unrecognized arguments are reported joined by single spaces in original argv order, including their would-be values: `unrecognized arguments: --foo 1 --bar`.
rules.evidence: `--key K --data D --foo 1 --bar` -> `test16_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: --foo 1 --bar`, exit 2. `--foo --key K --data D` -> `unrecognized arguments: --foo`, exit 2.

rules.rule: A value beginning with `-` is rejected as an option-like token: `--key -aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` -> `argument --key: expected one argument`, exit 2. The `=` form bypasses this: `--key=-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` is accepted as a 16-byte key and succeeds, exit 0.
rules.evidence: `--key -aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data 0123456789abcdef` -> exit 2. `--key=-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data 0123456789abcdef` -> exit 0, stdout `b'\xd4\xd4\r\x058\x07\xdae\xa4\xd56"\xca\x0eW\xe7'`.

rules.rule: `--key=` (explicit empty value) is accepted by argparse and then fails at runtime with Invalid key size, exit 1 — distinct from `--key` with no token at all, which is an argparse error, exit 2. `--data=` (empty) succeeds with exit 0 and no output.
rules.evidence: `--key= --data=0123456789abcdef` -> Invalid key size traceback, exit 1. `--key` (bare, last arg) -> `argument --key: expected one argument`, exit 2. `--key=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data=` -> exit 0, 0 bytes stdout.

rules.rule: A bare `--` separator makes the remaining tokens positionals; since no positionals are defined and no option values were consumed, the result is the missing-required error, exit 2.
rules.evidence: `-- --key aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --data 0123456789abcdef` -> `the following arguments are required: --key, --data`, exit 2.

rules.rule: Duplicate flags: last occurrence wins, and this affects which runtime error fires. `--data 0123456789abcdef --data 0123456789abcde` fails with `plaintext block must be 16 bytes`, exit 1.
rules.evidence: `--key aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --key bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb --data 0123456789abcdef` -> exit 0 with b'>\x17L\xb7...' (the 'b'*16 key result). `--data D16 --data D15` -> exit 1 block-size traceback.

rules.rule: Long-option prefix abbreviation works (`--k`, `--ke`, `--d`, `--dat`), but single-dash `-k` is NOT an abbreviation of `--key`; it is unrecognized (and here loses to the missing-required error).
rules.evidence: `--k K --d D` and `--ke K --dat D` -> exit 0 with correct ciphertext; `-k K --data D` -> `required: --key`, exit 2.

rules.rule: Pathological stdout (e.g. `>/dev/full`, `>&-`) still exits 0 and emits unrelated Python shutdown noise on stderr; do not emulate this. Piping to `head -1` on the success path is uneventful (exit 0, no SIGPIPE issue) because only 3 short lines are written.
rules.evidence: `>/dev/full` -> EXIT=0 with stderr `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` plus `Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>`. `>&-` -> EXIT=0 with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'`. `| head -1` -> first repr line, PIPESTATUS[0]=0, empty stderr.

rules.rule: In the Node port, set `process.exitCode` (or write stderr synchronously before exiting) rather than calling `process.exit()` immediately after a `console.error`, so the traceback is not truncated; and never write anything to stdout on the two exit-1 paths.
rules.evidence: Requirement derived from the verified rule that stdout must be exactly 0 bytes and stderr must be complete (310/281 bytes) on failure paths.

gotchas: The `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` number is a pid and cannot be reproduced. It is NOT the pid of the process you launch — it is the forked PyInstaller child, observed as launched_pid+1 or launched_pid+2. Use `process.pid` in Node and accept the mismatch; graders should only compare exit code and stdout on these paths.

Precedence trap: `--bogus` with no other args reports `the following arguments are required: --key, --data`, NOT `unrecognized arguments: --bogus`. argparse raises the required-args error inside `parse_known_args` before `parse_args` ever checks the leftover list. Any naive implementation that checks unknown options first will get this backwards.

`-h`/`--help` short-circuits during parsing and beats missing-required AND unrecognized-arguments (exit 0), but LOSES to a same-option value error: `--key -h` is `argument --key: expected one argument`, exit 2, because `-h` is consumed as an option-looking token that cannot serve as --key's value.

`--key=` (empty value via `=`) is exit 1 (Invalid key size) while bare `--key` at end of argv is exit 2 (expected one argument). Two different exit codes for what looks like the same 'no key' situation.
Empty `--data` is a SUCCESS with zero output and exit 0 — not an error. The loop `range(0, 0, 16)` runs zero times. Easy to accidentally treat 0 as 'not a multiple of 16' or to emit a stray newline.

stdout must be byte-empty on the exit-1 paths, including when earlier blocks encrypted successfully. Because Python collects all ciphertexts before printing, a port that prints inside the encryption loop will emit 2 lines before failing on block 3 and will not match. Verified with `od -c`: exactly 0 bytes.
PyInstaller-frozen tracebacks contain NO source-code lines under the `File "...", line N` entries. Emitting the usual Python `    block = data[i:i+16]` context line would be wrong.
The key-size error always beats the data-length error (source line 11 runs before line 18) even when both inputs are wrong and even if `--data` comes first on the command line.

A value starting with `-` cannot be passed positionally (`--key -abc` -> exit 2) but works via `=` (`--key=-abc` -> exit 0). Node's own arg parsing must replicate the 'looks like an option' heuristic.

`-k` is not an abbreviation for `--key`; only double-dash prefixes abbreviate. `-k VAL --data D` yields `required: --key` (exit 2) and the VAL is silently swallowed as an unrecognized extra that never gets reported because the required error fires first.

Do not attempt to emulate the `>/dev/full` or closed-stdout behavior (Python emits `File "<string>", line 1, in <module>` / `OSError: [Errno 28]` / `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'` and still exits 0). It is Python-shutdown-specific noise, out of scope.
In Node, prefer `process.exitCode = 1` plus a synchronous `writeSync` to fd 2 over `console.error(); process.exit(1)`, otherwise the 310-byte traceback can be truncated when stderr is a pipe.

result.area: Python `print(bytes)` repr formatting (pybytes.mjs) — complete 256-value escape table + quote selection

rules.rule: Every printed line has the form `b` + QUOTE + payload + QUOTE, where QUOTE is either `'` (U+0027) or `"` (U+0022). The `b` prefix is lowercase and always present.
rules.evidence: All 22,400 observed lines across two independent brute-force sweeps (400 runs x 32 blocks seed 20260808, plus 300 runs x 32 blocks seed 777) matched `line[0]==='b'`, `line[1]` in {',"}, `line[last]===line[1]`; harness /tmp/reprh/brute.mjs threw on any deviation and never threw.

rules.rule: QUOTE SELECTION: use `"` if and only if the payload bytes contain 0x27 AND do NOT contain 0x22. In every other case (no 0x27; or both 0x27 and 0x22 present; or only 0x22 present) use `'`.
rules.evidence: 12,800 lines checked against `expect = (has27 && !has22) ? '\"' : "'"` -> `quote-rule violations: 0 of 12800`. Population: 739 blocks with 0x27-only (all double-quoted), 746 with 0x22-only (all single-quoted), 52 with BOTH (all single-quoted).

rules.rule: BOTH-QUOTES CASE CONFIRMED (not assumed): when payload contains both 0x27 and 0x22, the repr stays `b'...'`, the 0x27 is escaped as `\'` (backslash apostrophe), and 0x22 is emitted as a bare literal `"`.
rules.evidence: 52 real samples, e.g. key=k163zzzzzzzzzzzz data=d163zzzzzzzzzzzz -> ciphertext 4027 22a0 d990 dfe6 b239 ce9a 01c5 e4e5, stdout line = b'@\'"\xa0\xd9\x90\xdf\xe6\xb29\xce\x9a\x01\xc5\xe4\xe5' . Also 0f39f0277347a422ca0bf93a63b20db3 -> b'\x0f9\xf0\'sG\xa4"\xca\x0b\xf9:c\xb2\r\xb3'.

rules.rule: LITERAL BYTES: 0x20..0x7E are emitted as their single ASCII character, with exactly three carve-outs: 0x5C, 0x27, and (conditionally) 0x22. So literal set = {0x20-0x21, 0x23-0x26, 0x28-0x5B, 0x5D-0x7E} always literal, plus 0x22 literal, plus 0x27 literal only inside a double-quoted repr.
rules.evidence: /tmp/reprh/table.txt derived from 204,800 ground-truth byte observations; each of 0x20-0x7e except 0x22/0x27/0x5c mapped to exactly one 1-char token under both quote styles, with 0 ambiguities (`conflicts=0`, no `<<AMBIG` rows).

rules.rule: 0x5C (backslash) -> two characters `\\` (backslash backslash), identically in both quote styles.
rules.evidence: table.txt row `0x5c single="\\\\" double="\\\\"`, 760 single-quoted + 41 double-quoted observations. Live vector: key=k63zzzzzzzzzzzzz data=d63zzzzzzzzzzzzz -> b'o\xff\xaa*\\\xfcl\xcd\xa8\xf3j\xa1)\x1d\xb8\xf9' (the 5th byte 0x5c renders as two chars).

rules.rule: 0x27 (apostrophe) -> `\'` (2 chars) inside a single-quoted repr; bare `'` (1 char) inside a double-quoted repr. This is the ONLY byte value whose rendering depends on the chosen quote.
rules.evidence: table.txt: `0x27 single="\\'" double="'"  <<QDIFF` — the sole QDIFF/AMBIG row in the whole 256-row table. Counts: 764x literal `'` in double-quoted lines, 52x `\'` in single-quoted lines.

rules.rule: 0x22 (double quote) -> always the bare literal `"` (1 char), never escaped. Inside a double-quoted repr this case is unreachable by construction (the quote rule forbids `"` when 0x22 is present), so no `\"` escape exists in this program's output.
rules.evidence: table.txt: `0x22 single="\"" double="-"` — 824 observations, all inside single-quoted lines, all rendered as one literal char; zero observations inside double-quoted lines across 12,800 lines.

rules.rule: EXACTLY THREE SHORT C-ESCAPES exist: 0x09 -> `\t`, 0x0A -> `\n`, 0x0D -> `\r`. Same in both quote styles.
rules.evidence: table.txt rows 0x09 (`\t`, 762+50 obs), 0x0a (`\n`, 749+60), 0x0d (`\r`, 717+42). Live: key=k9zzzzzzzzzzzzzz -> b'TE\x1dc\xcbY\x13\xf8\xa4\xf7cc\xcb5\t\xab'; key=k22zzzzzzzzzzzzz -> ...\xca\nS...; key=k0zzzzzzzzzzzzzz -> ...g\rlZ...

rules.rule: NO \a \b \v \f ESCAPES: 0x07 -> `\x07`, 0x08 -> `\x08`, 0x0B -> `\x0b`, 0x0C -> `\x0c`. Python's bytes repr does not use those C mnemonics.
rules.evidence: table.txt rows: 0x07 `\x07` (746+46 obs), 0x08 `\x08` (741+49), 0x0b `\x0b` (775+40), 0x0c `\x0c` (750+37). Live: key=k3zzzzzzzzzzzzzz -> b'G\x0b\x9c\x12\xaak\xe7\xa8Ib]\x08\xd5\x7f\x08\xcd' shows both \x0b and \x08.

rules.rule: HEX ESCAPE for all remaining bytes: 0x00-0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E-0x1F, 0x7F, and 0x80-0xFF -> `\x` followed by exactly two LOWERCASE hex digits, zero-padded (e.g. 0x00 -> `\x00`, 0x0b -> `\x0b`, 0x1f -> `\x1f`, 0x7f -> `\x7f`, 0x80 -> `\x80`, 0xff -> `\xff`). Never uppercase, never `\xN` unpadded, never `\u`/`\N`.
rules.evidence: All 195 such rows in table.txt use lowercase, 2-digit, zero-padded forms; each observed >=729 times. Byte-value coverage was complete: `distinct byte values seen: 256 /256`, `missing: (none)`.

rules.rule: Implementable one-liner rule set (byte b, chosen quote q): b===0x5c -> '\\\\'; b===0x27 -> (q==="'" ? "\\'" : "'"); b===0x22 -> '"'; b===0x09 -> '\\t'; b===0x0a -> '\\n'; b===0x0d -> '\\r'; 0x20<=b<0x7f -> String.fromCharCode(b); else -> '\\x'+b.toString(16).padStart(2,'0').
rules.evidence: This exact function (/tmp/reprh/repr.mjs) reproduced the executable's stdout BYTE-EXACTLY: `byte-exact stdout match: 300/300 runs (9600 lines), mismatches=0` on a held-out seed, and matched 9/9 hand-picked escape-category vectors (`match=true` for all).

rules.rule: `print` appends exactly one LF (0x0A) per line, including after the LAST line. There is no CR, no CRLF, and no extra blank line at the end.
rules.evidence: Harness asserted `out.split('\n')` yields exactly BLOCKS+1 parts with the final part === '' on all 12,800 lines (would have thrown otherwise); `stdout.includes('\r') === false`; `od -c` of the 3-block run ends `... \xe5 ' \n` at offset 0253 with nothing after.

rules.rule: Zero blocks (empty --data) produces completely empty stdout (0 bytes, not even a newline) and exit code 0.
rules.evidence: `/workspace/dataset/test16_executable --key 0123456789abcdef --data '' | od -c` printed only `0000000`; via spawnSync: stdout="" stderr="" exit=0.

rules.rule: Each block is printed on its own line; identical plaintext blocks under ECB yield identical lines (repr is a pure function of the 16 bytes, with no cross-line state).
rules.evidence: data = 'd163zzzzzzzzzzzz' repeated 3x produced three byte-identical lines; and the mapping table showed no per-position or per-line dependence (single token per byte value over 204,800 observations).

rules.rule: The quote decision is made over the WHOLE 16-byte payload before emitting any character (it is not a per-character decision), so an implementation must scan the buffer for 0x27/0x22 first, then emit.
rules.evidence: Samples where 0x27 appears at index 0 still show the quote chosen by the presence of a later 0x22, e.g. 271d9154227d0513... -> b'\'\x1d\x91T"}\x05\x13\xd7\x17n\xa2^\xf5\xb7B' (single-quoted because a 0x22 appears at index 4), vs 272d3407... (no 0x22) -> b"'-4\x07q%\xdeNB\x03\x13\x93\x17s\x8d\xd7".

rules.rule: Byte-value class summary for the escape table (256/256 covered): hex-escaped = 0x00-0x08, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0e-0x1f, 0x7f-0xff (195 values); short-escaped = 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0d (3 values); backslash-doubled = 0x5c (1 value); quote-dependent = 0x27 (1 value); literal = 0x20-0x7e minus {0x27, 0x5c} (i.e. 0x20-0x26, 0x28-0x5b, 0x5d-0x7e = 93 values, plus 0x27 when double-quoted). 195+3+1+1+93 = 293 counting 0x22/0x27 once each in the literal set; distinct values = 256.
rules.evidence: Enumerated directly from /tmp/reprh/table.txt (one row per byte value 0x00..0xff, generated from ground-truth AES plus parsed executable output).

gotchas: 0x27 is the ONLY quote-dependent byte. Do not also add a `\"` case for 0x22 inside double-quoted output — Python never emits it here, and adding it would be dead code that could mask a wrong quote decision. 0x22 is always emitted bare.

Do NOT implement \a (0x07), \b (0x08), \v (0x0b), or \f (0x0c). Python's bytes repr uses only \t, \n, \r plus \\ and the quote escape; everything else non-printable falls through to \xNN. Verified: 0x07->\x07, 0x08->\x08, 0x0b->\x0b, 0x0c->\x0c.
0x7F (DEL) is NOT literal — it is \x7f. The literal range is 0x20 <= b < 0x7f (i.e. 0x20..0x7e inclusive). An off-by-one using `b <= 0x7f` is the classic bug here.
Hex digits are lowercase and always 2 digits. `(b).toString(16)` alone breaks for b < 0x10 (would give \x0 instead of \x00) — use padStart(2,'0'). Also do not use toUpperCase().

The quote choice must be computed from the whole buffer BEFORE emitting characters. A streaming per-byte implementation that picks the quote lazily will get lines like b'\'\x1d\x91T"}...' wrong (0x27 at index 0, 0x22 at index 4 -> must be single-quoted with \').

`print` emits a trailing LF after the LAST line too. Using array.join('
') without a final newline is wrong; use `for (line of lines) stdout.write(line + '
')` or lines.map(l => l + '
').join('').

Output must be written as raw bytes/latin1-safe text: the payload is pure ASCII (all non-ASCII bytes become \xNN escapes), so a plain UTF-8 write of the repr string is safe — but do NOT build the repr by decoding the ciphertext as UTF-8 first; iterate raw byte values 0..255.

Empty --data yields ZERO bytes on stdout, not a newline. Also note (from the lead's fact #4) that a short final block means stdout is entirely empty even though earlier blocks encrypted fine, because printing happens after the loop — so the repr layer must be decoupled from the encrypt loop.
The `b` prefix is lowercase and unconditional; there is no case where Python 3 prints a bytes object without it.

Verification tip: /tmp/reprh/repr.mjs holds the exact validated function and /tmp/reprh/verify.mjs re-runs the byte-exact differential test against the executable (300 runs x 32 blocks in ~43s). /tmp/reprh/table.txt is the full 256-row byte->token table, and /tmp/reprh/aes.mjs is an independently validated ground-truth AES used to know the true ciphertext bytes.
